rationale:
OWNER REPORT 2026-08-25: 'a couple of the pages have no hero images which has meant that the copy is also unreadable. e.g. services.html'. His causal reading is correct and the cause is a shared platform seam, not his site.

`cta_bg` is the one palette slot whose contract admits a GRADIENT as well as a colour (derive_brand_head_assets_action.go:275 documents that shape as expected; 10 of the fleet's css_themes hold one, MEASURED 2026-08-25). Five live component rows substitute that token into positions requiring a <color>: three hero bands put it in a gradient colour-STOP and inside color-mix(), and two CTA buttons use it as a `color:` value. A gradient in a <color> position is INVALID AT COMPUTED-VALUE TIME, so the declaration is discarded and the property falls back to inherit/initial -- crucially NOT to the earlier valid declaration in the same rule. The hero's own safety net (`background: var(--color-cta-bg, var(--color-primary))` on the line above) is therefore defeated by the line meant to enhance it, and the button's ink falls back to the band's inherited white.

Measured on the live estate with scripts/render_audit.py (VIZ-010), 2026-08-25: finetuning.uk/services.html and /about.html hero H1 at 1.11:1 (needs 3.0); A.cta-btn at 1.00:1 (needs 4.5) on those two AND on the site's paid front door /your-own-model.html; robot-hands.com/about.html reproduces the 1.00:1 independently.

Why the pages with images are fine: the hero template takes an imaged branch (dark scrim + inline --hero-ink:#fff) whenever the page has a hero image, so only an image-less page reaches the broken band. That is why the owner saw the two facts as one.

The estate ALREADY detected this and lost it: 11 contrast_failure rows were filed for finetuning.uk on 2026-08-10, including the 1.11:1 H1s, carrying the invented `H1.H1` selector (bugs_closed/352); they sat `deferred` for two weeks and were cancelled wholesale by migration 587 on 2026-08-24 without ever being repaired.

The fix reuses the existing legible-ink companion mechanism (VIZ-014) rather than inventing a parallel concept, because this IS that mechanism's problem statement -- 'a palette colour used as a FILL and the same colour used as an INK are different questions'.

plan.summary: Add --color-cta-bg-ink as a fourth legible-ink companion (source = cta_bg reduced to a solid, ground = the inverted button's cta_text face), and stop five component rows using --color-cta-bg in a <color> position.

edits.rationale: Append a fourth companion after the existing `wanted` slice. Construction is identical to the --color-accent-text entry directly above it (an ink for text on a filled control), mirrored because here the FILL colour is what must be re-tinted. Emitted ONLY when cta_text is known: with no measurable ground, legibleInkFor's terminal branch compares worstRatioAgainst('#ffffff') with worstRatioAgainst('#000000'), both return 0, `0 >= 0` holds and it hands back WHITE -- which on a white button face IS the 1.00:1 defect being repaired. That is not theoretical: removing the guard in mutation M1 emitted exactly #ffffff.

cta_bg is the one slot that may be a gradient, so every consumer needing a <color> comes through solidCTAFill; a caller reading palette["cta_bg"] directly is the defect. firstGradientStop is deliberately narrow -- hex stops only, which is what all 10 gradient themes actually hold (MEASURED 2026-08-25). Returning "" for rgb()/hsl()/named stops is the safe direction: the companion is then not emitted, every consumer falls through its own var() fallback, and behaviour is exactly today's. Widening it must bring its own contrast measurement.

Seven tests on live fleet palettes, not synthetic ones, chosen because they DISAGREE: finetuning's #1e40af already clears the target on white and must survive untouched; default/robot-hands' #3b82f6 does not and must be re-tinted. A suite carrying only one of them would pass against an implementation that always substitutes, or one that never does. Two mutations run and reverted: (M1) drop the cta_text guard -> NoCTAInkWithoutAGround FAILED, emitting #ffffff, the predicted vacuous white; (M2) make legibleInkFor always keep its source -> CTAInkRetintsAnIllegibleFirstStop FAILED on the raw #3b82f6 at 3.68:1 while CTAInkKeepsALegibleFirstStop stayed green.

edits.symbol: content_components: about-hero, contact-hero, services-hero, call-to-action, tool-cta
edits.rationale: Heroes: DELETE the second `background:` declaration. The valid single declaration is already on the line above and covers both a gradient and a colour; the deleted line was cosmetic (an 82% color-mix toward the ink). The sibling heroes `hero`, `use-cases-hero` and `case-studies-hero` carry the SAME idiom against --color-primary, which is always a colour -- they are correct and are deliberately untouched, and they are the in-repo control for this diagnosis. Buttons: repoint the ink at var(--color-cta-bg-ink, var(--color-cta-bg)) -- the mandatory two-level form of the ink contract (inkPolicy.enabled's comment records 46 consumer rows, 0 bare), so this half is a NO-OP until the chassis roll emits the token and degrades to today's behaviour if the ink kill-switch is thrown. Needles were extracted from the live rows, not retyped; each matches exactly once.
edits.sketch:
UPDATE content_components SET html_template = replace(html_template,
  E'\n    background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--color-cta-bg, var(--color-primary)) 0%, color-mix(...) 100%);', '')
 WHERE name IN ('about-hero','contact-hero','services-hero') AND html_template LIKE '%...%';
-- + 2 button UPDATEs, + a DO/RAISE verify block

edits.rationale: A DO/RAISE, not a block of SELECTs: ON_ERROR_STOP does not treat a non-empty result as an error, so a SELECT-only verify cannot stop the COMMIT. INDUCED against pre-migration state -- the colour-stop arm RAISEd, and that is how a FOURTH row was found at all: my by-name census had encoded its own answer. Arms 2 and 4 read 2 and 0 pre-migration (both would raise); arm 3 reads 3 before and after and is stated as a post-condition against OVER-deletion rather than something that can fire early. The color-mix arm is PINNED at exactly 1 rather than cleared: tool-password-entropy_pre_037 has the same invalid-value fault but its harm is a missing panel tint, not unreadable text, and it has ZERO page_components uses -- repairing it needs a solid FILL companion, a different token from this legible INK, with no live consumer, which is the accumulating-opt-in-surface shape RFC_022 discourages. It is recorded as a known remainder in bugs_open/398, and the pin means a NEW component taking the same wrong turn refuses the migration rather than passing unnoticed.
edits.sketch:
IF n_band2 <> 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '619: % component(s) still substitute --color-cta-bg into a gradient stop', n_band2; END IF;
IF n_mix <> 1 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '619: % use --color-cta-bg inside color-mix(), want exactly the 1 known unshipped row', n_mix; END IF;

edits.rationale: Restores the exact prior bytes, and says plainly in its header that doing so restores the DEFECT. Guarded so it cannot double-apply (the hero arm requires the gradient-stop line to be absent).

grounded_in: scripts/render_audit.py, finetuning.uk/services.html, 2026-08-25: '1.11:1 need 3.0  rgb(255, 255, 255) on rgb(245,243,239)  .hero-content H1' -- the measured background is the PAGE cream, neither the blue gradient nor the --color-primary fallback, which is what identifies the declaration as invalid rather than merely ugly.
scripts/render_audit.py, finetuning.uk/your-own-model.html, 2026-08-25: '1.00:1 need 4.5  rgb(255, 255, 255) on rgb(255,255,255)  A.cta-btn' -- on the site's paid front door.
CONTROL, same component family, non-imaged branch, SOLID cta_bg (#e9e2d3): noted.co.uk/contact.html has ZERO hero contrast failures. The only variable is the token's type.
SECOND SITE: robot-hands.com/about.html, 'A.cta-btn 1.00:1' -- the defect is not finetuning-specific.

derive_brand_head_assets_action.go:275: 'Gradient values (e.g. cta_bg) are rejected by parseHexColour downstream.' -- the platform already treats a gradient cta_bg as an expected shape, so the components are wrong, not the palette.

css_themes, MEASURED 2026-08-25: 10 themes hold a gradient --color-cta-bg (calm-minimal, dark-modern, default, professional-dark, tech, warm-friendly, finetuning-uk, gaswholesalers-com, loanandmortgagecalculator-co-uk, robot-hands-com); 4 more matched a looser LIKE and are solid.

The first gradient stop is NOT an ink: against a white button face #3b82f6 scores 3.68, #059669 3.82, #8b5cf6 4.28 -- 6 of the 10 themes below AA. Only #1e40af (8.8) would have made the naive fix look correct, and that is the theme in front of me.

palette_specialised_slots.go, inkPolicy.enabled: 'MEASURED 2026-08-14 across content_components, site_components, layouts and page_components: 46 rows reference an ink var, 0 of them bare' -- the two-level var(--ink, var(--raw)) form this change follows.

site_work_items, finetuning.uk: 11 contrast_failure rows created 2026-08-10; the three 1.11:1 H1 rows carry item_key 'contrast_failure:/about.html#H1.H1' and are 'cancelled' (migration 587, 2026-08-24); seven A.cta-btn 1.00:1 rows are still 'deferred'.
plan.risks:
The button half is INERT until the next chassis roll -- var(--color-cta-bg-ink, var(--color-cta-bg)) resolves to the gradient until the renderer emits the companion, i.e. exactly today's behaviour. Deliberate: the alternative fallbacks were measured and all fail. --color-primary is illegible on a white button on 4 of 12 themes (theme-loanandmortgagecalculator-co-uk scores 1.24:1, trading one invisible button for another), and the raw first stop fails on 6 of 10. There is no correct token until this one exists.

The hero half is live on the next re-render of any page using those three components, across every site, not just finetuning.uk. On a solid-cta_bg site the visible change is losing a subtle 82% gradient sheen on the band; the fill colour is unchanged because the surviving declaration is the same token.

Re-render required: content_components is the template, the served pages hold rendered output. A page_rerender re-assembles from content_data plus the template, so the CSS updates and the copy is not regenerated -- which is what makes this compatible with the finetuning lane's standing copy hold.

firstGradientStop is narrow by construction and silently emits nothing for an rgb()/hsl()/named-colour stop. Today that set is empty; if a future palette uses one, the affected consumers revert to present-day behaviour rather than breaking, but the repair will not reach them and nothing will say so.

tool-password-entropy_pre_037 keeps three invalid color-mix() backgrounds. Unshipped (0 page_components uses) and a different harm class; pinned by the verify block and recorded in bugs_open/398 rather than fixed silently.
